formalDefinition: For a weighted graph G= (V,E) with non-negative edge weights, a source vertex s ∈ V, and a target vertex t ∈ V, find the shortest path from s to t, where path length is defined as the sum of edge weights along the path.
problemDefinition: Single Pair Shortest Path (SPSP) in a weighted graph is the problem of finding the shortest path from a given source vertex s and target vertex t in the graph, such that the sum of edge weights along the path is minimized.
inputDescription: A weighted graph with a source vertex and a target vertex
outputDescription: The shortest path from the source vertex to the target vertex, or empty if unreachable
instanceFormat: Format: (N,E,s,t) | s,t in N, optional (default to the first/last node of N when omitted); N,E parsed as one of: {(N,E) | N is set, E subset {(e,w) | e is N cross N, w is int}} | {(N,E) | N is set, E subset {(e,w) | e is N unorderedcross N, w is int}} | {(N,E) | N is set, E subset N cross N} | {(N,E) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N} Example: ({1,2,3,4,5},{((1,2),4),((1,3),2),((2,3),1),((3,5),7),((2,4),3),((4,5),9)},1,5) Parallel edges: when two edges join the same nodes (in the same direction, if directed), the lightest one is used.
certificateFormat: Format: {q0,...,qn} | qi are node names, q0 = s, qn = t, each (qi,qi+1) in E; {} (no path) is never a valid certificate Example: {1,3,5}

defaultVerifier.verifierName: Default Single Pair Shortest Path Problem Verifier
defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: Verifies the solution for the Single Pair Shortest Path problem

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Visualizes the Single Pair Shortest Path problem for non-negative weighted directed cyclic graphs using Dijkstra's algorithm
